![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/57ba7828008f3e3c271ae4c1b6d444005f40c09bf6ba99e614f3b6414c1e56c2.png)

An employee of a car dealership collects data on the value $y$ (in thousands of dollars) of a particular car model $t$ years after its release to the market. The residual plot above was constructed after fitting a linear regression model on this data set. Which of the following statements are true?

I. When $t=6,$ the regression equation overestimates the value of $y.$

II. The residuals appear randomly scattered about the horizontal axis (there are no obvious trends).

III. This linear regression is probably a good fit for the data.
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. The residual equals the actual value minus the estimated value:

$$
\text{Residual}=\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated}
$$

 
From the plot, the residual at $t=6$ is negative. So, we have that $\text{Actual}<\text{Estimated},$ and therefore the model overestimates this data point.

- Statement II is false. The plot shows the residuals tend to decrease as time increases. So, there is a trend, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14233881/assets/fe18ccc94d0cc98f971b6482d4e31c7ec7066b5cec427108ddd8d1e6609e08ba.png)

  

- Statement III is false. Since the residuals are *not* randomly scattered above and below the horizontal axis, our regression line is *not* a good fit for the given data.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
